newsitem.title: USA: Lucent adds Westell technology to local loops.
newsitem.headline: Lucent adds Westell technology to local loops.

text.p: Lucent Technologies Inc said Tuesday it would add Westell Technologies Inc's technology for sending high-speed data over standard copper phone lines to the local phone equipment it supplies carriers.

Lucent said it planned to integrate the Westell technology -- known as Advanced Digital Subscriber Line (ADSL) -- into its digital local loop carrier systems, which are the most widely used local phone systems in the United States.
Lucent's local loop systems -- used to connect local phone customers to phone company central offices -- are supplied to all of the Baby Bells and GTE Corp.

A Lucent spokeswoman said the pact would allow the company to have digital subscriber line products available by the second quarter of 1998 that are capable of transmitting data at speeds of up to six megabits to residential customers. That is 100 to 200 times faster than the technology now typically used by home computer users to connect to the Interent over standard phone lines.

Lucent said such high-speed data services could be added incrementally by local phone carriers based on customer demand. Service providers simply "plug in" the new product into their existing digital local service phone systems.
More than 25 million customers receive their local phone connections via Lucent digital loop carrier systems.
On the receiving end, Lucent said its systems would be designed to work with high-speed Westell modems located in the customer's home or business.

The new systems would be designed to satisfy the growing demand for high-speed data transmission from customers who work out of their home and Internet users who seek want rapid access to high-resolution graphics over the World Wide Web.

Lucent, which is the former AT&T equipment arm, said similar capabilities, using Westell's multiplexer version of its product, can be used in Lucent's system for providing a range of new broadband services to local phone customers.
The company has developed such systems jointly with BroadBand Technologies Inc, it said.
Lucent already has announced plans to incorporate a slightly different DSL technology developed by Paradyne, another former AT&T subsidary, into Lucent's data networking product line.
The Paradyne product is targetted mainly at small business customers, Lucent said.
